introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: answer ALL 2 questions. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K. Relative atomic masses: H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, Cl = 35.5, Ag = 108.

questions.enonce_markdown: Ethanol to ethanoic acid ($\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}$ to $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$). *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reaction type: oxidation.**

**Reagent:** an oxidising agent, **acidified potassium dichromate(VI)** (or acidified potassium permanganate) in excess.

**Conditions:** warm the mixture and **heat under reflux** (so that the volatile ethanol and its intermediate product are not lost) until the oxidation is complete.

**Equation** (oxygen supplied by the oxidising agent, written [O]):

$\mathrm{C_2H_5OH} + 2[\mathrm{O}] \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3COOH} + \mathrm{H_2O}$

With dichromate: $3\mathrm{C_2H_5OH} + 2\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}} + 16\mathrm{H^+} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{CH_3COOH} + 4\mathrm{Cr^{3+}} + 11\mathrm{H_2O}$

**Observation:** the orange solution turns **green**.

**Reaction type: substitution** (free radical substitution): one hydrogen atom of methane is replaced by a chlorine atom.

**Reagent:** **chlorine gas**, $\mathrm{Cl_2}$.

**Conditions:** **ultraviolet light** (or bright sunlight) at room temperature; methane is in excess to limit further substitution.

**Equation:**

$\mathrm{CH_4} + \mathrm{Cl_2} \xrightarrow{\;\text{UV light}\;} \mathrm{CH_3Cl} + \mathrm{HCl}$

(With more chlorine the substitution continues to $\mathrm{CH_2Cl_2}$, $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ and $\mathrm{CCl_4}$.)

**Reaction type: addition** (hydrogenation): hydrogen adds across the $\mathrm{C=C}$ double bond, which becomes a single bond.

**Reagent:** **hydrogen gas**, $\mathrm{H_2}$.

**Conditions:** a **finely divided nickel catalyst** at about **150 $^\circ$C**.

**Equation:**

$\mathrm{C_2H_4} + \mathrm{H_2} \xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{Ni},\ 150^\circ\mathrm{C}\;} \mathrm{C_2H_6}$

questions.enonce_markdown: Ethanoic acid to ethyl ethanoate ($\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ to $\mathrm{CH_3COOC_2H_5}$). *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reaction type: esterification** (condensation: two molecules join and water is lost).

**Reagent:** **ethanol**, $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}$.

**Conditions:** a few drops of **concentrated sulphuric acid as catalyst**, and **warm gently (heat under reflux)**. The reaction is reversible.

**Equation:**

$\mathrm{CH_3COOH} + \mathrm{C_2H_5OH} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CH_3COOC_2H_5} + \mathrm{H_2O}$

The ester is a sweet-smelling (fruity) liquid.
